To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the microarchitecture of human cancellous tissue is related to the structural integrity of bone and that the fracture toughness of the bone is dependent upon the microarchitecture and bone tissue properties.
1. The fracture toughness of osteoporotic human cancellous bone tissue is correlated with the bone microarchitecture parameters of bone volume fraction (BV/TV), bone surface area to tissue
BV/TV, BS/BV, TbN, SMI and BMD are all important parameters that can be used to predict the fracture resistance (FT) of cancellous tissue.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between the microstructure of cancellous bone and its mechanical properties.
the development and application of novel methods to study the microstructure and fracture properties of osteoporotic cancellus bone in a human population.
understanding the microstructural and micro-mechanical properties of human cancellous tissue in relation to fracture toughness and the potential to improve clinical assessment of fracture risk.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fracture toughness of cancellous bone tissue is influenced by both the microarchitecture and the tissue properties.
the microarchitecture parameters of TbTh, TbN and SMI are the most important in the context of bone strength and fracture toughness.
BV/TV is a good indicator of bone quality and fracture toughness.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that the structural integrity and toughness of osteoporotic cancellus bone is related to the microarchitecture of the tissue and this may have important consequences for the development of new bone therapies.
the micro architecture of cancellous bone is a key parameter that needs to be included in any model of bone strength and fracture risk.

BV/TV is the most important microarchitecture parameter for the structural integrity of osteoporotic cancellus bone, but it is not sufficient alone and that other microarchitecture parameters such as BS/BV, BS/TV and SMI are important and may be used as surrogates for BV/TV to improve fracture prediction.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the microarchitecture parameters TbTh, TbN, SMI and BS/BV are more strongly correlated with FT than is BV/TV, and therefore could be used in the future to improve the prediction of fracture risk in osteoporotic patients.

the microarchitectural parameter, TbN (Tissue Number) is a good predictor of bone strength in osteoporotic tissue, and is the only one of those investigated that can be measured from a 2D image of the bone.
the microarchitecture is important in fracture prediction and that it can be assessed from a combination of parameters that are easily measured using standard techniques.
